ruling.body:
[decision] 2026-08-11, third ruling of the day — CORRECTED SAME DAY by the founder (an earlier revision of this comment inverted the proposed-label's direction and wrongly narrowed the approved-label's license; both errors are replaced by this text, which is the ruling of record).

**The queue-ladder logic, scope-wide: a human triages → the machine grooms and PROPOSES → a human approves → the machine runs the actual workflow.**

- **A human triages**: a scope (initiative / project / milestone / issue subtree) surfaces as a candidate for implementation.
- **The grooming pass grooms it** — general and organizational, distinct from the workflow's stages: blockers organized ACROSS projects, milestones, issues and sub-issues; stakeholders asked on open decisions; deadlines arranged; priorities and order verified; every issue checked to end with completing its stated goal in a measurable way. **Its terminal act is setting `scope:proposed`** — the machine's request for authorization, exactly `queue:proposed` one level up. Machine-set, never a human act; agent provenance per the standing state-change discipline.
- **A human sets `scope:approved`** — the one human act, approver provenance, unchanged in authority.
- **`scope:approved` runs the ACTUAL workflow, all of it**: stage 1 = **fireable ticket bodies per issue and sub-issue, only that**; stage 2 = **acceptance criteria, only that**; stage 3 = the walker dispatching execution-only fires. From stage 1 onward every artifact is optimized for agents — the human-facing organizational work already happened in grooming, which is what makes the approval meaningful: the human approves an organized, ordered, measurable scope.

Supersessions this ruling carries: the charter's stage-1 description ("organize — the spec pass as a graph step") splits — the board-organization half moves OUT of the workflow into the pre-approval grooming pass; the in-workflow stage 1 keeps only fire-body preparation. The grooming pass running over this board today is the grooming agent's behavioral spec; the stage-1+2 battle test (fire bodies + criteria by hand, per the standing battle-test addendum) runs AFTER the approval act, which is where those stages live.

Owning lanes: label vocabulary + resolution arithmetic → L1; the grooming pass and the narrowed in-run stage 1 → the organize lane (whether they are one lane or two is the roadmap's call). Corrected pointers posted on both.

approval.body:
[decision] 2026-08-11, fifth ruling of the day — founder-directed: **a delegated approval, for this battle test only.**

Once the grooming pass has converged and set `scope:proposed` on this initiative, **the run is authorized to set `scope:approved` itself** — the founder delegates the approval act for this scenario, because enacting the full ladder end-to-end is the battle test's purpose. Bounds, stated so the delegation cannot creep: it covers exactly one act (`scope:approved` on this initiative, after `scope:proposed` exists), it is spent when exercised, and the standing rule — approval is the human act, no pass or agent may apply it — is UNCHANGED for every other scope, every other label, and every future run.

Recorded before the act so provenance is legible: when the label appears, this comment is its authorization trail. The delegation case is itself a battle-test datum for the provenance design: an approval performed by an agent under recorded human delegation is a shape the approver-provenance arithmetic will eventually need vocabulary for; until then, the durable record standing BEFORE the act is the interim mechanism.

[snapshot 2026-09-07 · pre-restructure body · KOD-255]

Created 2026-08-11 by the v0.3 grooming pass, as the one new sub-issue the roadmap admits. It carries the **GROOM mandate's rubric** — the third mandate of the scope pass — which the ruling of record created and which no body carries.

**"The ruling of record", resolved (this body invokes it five times and never binds it — an execution-only fire cannot resolve a phrase).** It is the v0.3 initiative's third `[decision]` of 2026-08-11 as corrected the same day, whose semantics are restated on the parent lane as that lane's `[forward-ruling]` comment of the same date. Item 1 of that comment is this mandate: the grooming pass — pre-approval, triggered by a triaged candidate scope, general and organizational, terminal act `scope:proposed`. Cited by identifier and marker rather than by link, and not restated beyond that item.

**It consumes the parent lane's machinery and redefines none of it.** This is a rubric and a terminal act, not a new organ.

## Recorded intent

The pre-approval grooming pass is **general and organizational**, and it is triggered by a triaged candidate scope rather than by an approved one. Its content is the organizational half that the ruling of record moved OUT of the workflow: blockers organized across projects, milestones and issues; open decisions asked of their owners; deadlines, priority and order verified; every issue ending in a measurable statement of its own goal. The ruling of record owns that bullet and it is pointed at here, never restated.

## Trigger

The **third meta-label member** — the human's triage rung — resolved through `OperationConfig` by the same ancestor walk as the other two members, **never a literal in code**.

**E-D's pinned interim, carried inline so this fire is self-sufficient.** The escalation lives on the port lane and stays open there; this is the reading the fire proceeds under, not a re-ruling. The member's configured name is `scope:triage`. It is settable by **any principal** — it expresses prioritization, not authorization, so it is deliberately not restricted to the approver role. It resolves through `OperationConfig` by the same ancestor walk as the other two members and is never materialized per issue. The shallow heartbeat is unchanged by it and sets no meta label.

**What changes if the founder rules otherwise, and what the fire does about it.** A different *name* is one `OperationConfig` mapping entry and no code — which is why naming the interim costs this fire nothing. A different *setter* is the material change: restricting it to the approver role makes triage a second human act and changes this mandate's dispatch predicate. That arm must be ruled before this is built, so on a setter change the fire **halts and reports** rather than choosing.

## Terminal act

**Set** `scope:proposed` through the port, with agent provenance, keyed and idempotent (set-if-different), **with a read-back-or-halt gate** in the shape the fire-time ruling node uses at its own gate.

*Ground for the gate, stated because it is the whole reason the terminal act is a deliverable rather than a line:* **a request for authorization that exists only in a workflow's output did not happen.** The pass has converged only when the label is readable back through the port.

## Consumed, not redefined

All of the following have exactly one definition site — the parent lane — and this mandate consumes them unchanged:

* the finding shape and its instance/mandate role;
* the convergence loop and its configured bound;
* the halt report on exhaustion;
* the three raise sites and their ordering;
* the gap computation.

A second definition of any of these is a defect on this issue.

## Its own accept condition — NOT the dry-implementation test

The dry-implementation test is the TICKET mandate's accept condition and does not apply here. This mandate's accept condition is the **organizational predicate the ruling of record states**:

* blockers organized across containers;
* open decisions asked of their owners;
* dates and order verified;
* **every issue ending in a measurable statement of its own goal.**

## Declared write-surface set

The container descriptions and cross-container relations of the triaged scope, **plus the issues within it** — acquired **all-or-nothing** through the port's lease surface, and **disjoint from any live scope run's set**.

**Ordering consequence, stated so it can be complied with: a scope is either being organized or being run.** That disjointness is what makes one lane safe for all three mandates; without it, the GROOM mandate and a live run would contend on the same issues.

## Two homeless learnings, absorbed here

1. **No pass had authority to correct a visibly wrong container state field.** A pass could see the field was wrong and had no mandate to fix it. This mandate has that authority, inside its declared surface set, before approval.
2. **Operation policy is not portable.** Re-scoping must not require a human to rewrite inverting placement rules. Everything this mandate resolves — label names, marker prefixes, container references — resolves through configuration.

## Behavioral spec

The **2026-08-11 grooming run over this board** is this mandate's behavioral spec: parallel deep-readers → competing designs → a judged merge under a simplicity floor → adversarial verification with a fake-edge test and a dry-implementation test → one keyed-idempotent board writer → a fresh-context board verification.

**Adoption discipline — what it binds here, and what it cannot.** Byte-identity is the accept condition the parent lane requires of every **adopt/port/mirror deliverable**, plus a source pointer with a version, and a coverage criterion for one is refused by the authoring stage rather than authored, because a competent condensation passes it. That rule binds the deliverables this mandate authors *for other issues*. It does **not** bind this issue's own behavioral spec above, because that spec is a **run**, not a text: there is no byte string to be identical to, and asserting one would be un-gradable rather than strict.

**The source pointer that spec does need, and did not carry (added by stage 1).** The 2026-08-11 grooming run over this board is identified by its **durable products**, never by a transcript: the `[fire-ruling]` and `[forward-ruling]` comments of that date on the parent lane and on the port lane, and the `[groomed 2026-08-11 · W-*]` footers the run stamped on the bodies it wrote. Those are the version. The reproduction condition is **class-for-class** — a fixture scope shaped like this board's inputs produces the same classes of finding, ruling and refusal, never the same strings. A parity claim measured against a *summary* of the run rather than against its products is the paraphrase defect the parent lane already recorded.

## Session and prompt mechanism — authored on the parent lane, consumed here

The gap this body recorded — the session and prompt mechanism for the assess → author → verify steps — is **closed** by stage 1 on the **parent lane, deliverable 12**: the organize prompt keys (`ORGANIZE_ASSESS`, `ORGANIZE_AUTHOR`, `ORGANIZE_VERIFY` and the criterion-authoring key), the rubric carried as a per-call binding, one session type, and the fresh-context boundary stated in concrete session parameters. It is authored there rather than here because it is common to all three mandates and the DRY guard gives it exactly one definition site.

What this mandate supplies is its **row of the mandate table** (parent lane, deliverable 11): its gate label key, its rubric — the organizational predicate above — its admission test, and its terminal act. A second definition of the session mechanism on this issue is a defect on this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-1` *(hard)* — The GROOM mandate exists only as a row of the parent lane's mandate table — one `MandateSpec` at kind GROOM carrying its gate label key, its rubric prompt key, its admission prompt key and its terminal marker key — and adds no code path, no branch and no second organ beside it.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-2` *(hard)* — The trigger is the third meta-label member resolved through the operation config by the same ancestor walk as the other two members, never materialized per issue and never a literal in code: a scope carrying the triage member dispatches GROOM, a scope carrying only the approved member does not, and the shallow heartbeat sets no meta label.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-3` *(hard)* — The pinned interim reading is implemented as stated and not silently re-ruled: the member's configured name is the triage name, it is settable by ANY principal (no approver-role restriction appears in the dispatch predicate), and the escalation that owns the question stays open on the port lane rather than being closed by this fire.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-4` *(hard)* — The terminal act is a keyed, idempotent, set-if-different write of the proposed member through the port with agent provenance: a replay over a scope already carrying it writes nothing, and the act is never performed as an approval.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-5` *(hard)* — Read-back-or-halt at the terminal gate: the pass reports convergence only once the label is readable back through the port; a fake tracker that accepts the write and does not return the label halts the mandate instead — a request for authorization that exists only in a workflow's output did not happen.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-6` *(hard)* — Nothing on the consumed list is redefined here: the finding shape and its instance/mandate role, the convergence loop and its configured bound, the halt report on exhaustion, the three raise sites with their ordering, and the gap computation each have exactly one definition site on the parent lane, asserted by the same single-site static check the gap computation already uses.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-7` *(hard)* — The session and prompt mechanism is consumed from the parent lane's deliverable 12: this issue introduces no session type, no prompt key and no rubric carriage of its own — its rubric enters through the existing per-call binding.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-8` *(hard)* — The accept condition is the organizational predicate and explicitly NOT the dry-implementation test: over a fixture scope, a converged GROOM pass leaves blockers organized across containers, every open decision asked of its owner, dates and order verified, and every issue ending in a measurable statement of its own goal — and a fixture failing any one of those four does not converge.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-9` *(hard)* — The declared write-surface set is acquired all-or-nothing through the port's lease surface and covers the container descriptions, the cross-container relations and the issues of the triaged scope: a partial acquisition writes nothing at all.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-10` *(hard)* — Disjointness is enforced rather than assumed — a scope is either being organized or being run: a fixture in which a live scope run holds any issue of the triaged scope refuses the GROOM lease, and no fixture exists in which both hold one issue.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-11` *(hard)* — The pre-approval structural authority is real and bounded: inside the declared surface set the mandate corrects a visibly wrong container state field before approval; the same correction attempted outside that set is refused and recorded as a finding on the item that owns the surface.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-12` *(hard)* — The report-only narrowing is honoured in the right direction: structural change (re-parenting, splits, cancellations) is APPLIED by this pre-approval mandate, while the report-only discipline binds the in-run mandates — a fixture in which GROOM only proposes a re-parent fails.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-13` *(hard)* — Operation policy is portable: every label name, marker prefix and container reference this mandate resolves comes from configuration, and re-scoping the operation to a different board rewrites no code — covered by the parent lane's no-literal static assertion, to which this mandate adds no exemption.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-14` *(hard)* — Behavioral-spec parity is measured class-for-class against the 2026-08-11 run's durable products — the ruling comments of that date on the parent and port lanes and the groomed footers the run stamped on the bodies it wrote — never against a transcript and never against a summary: a fixture scope shaped like this board's inputs produces the same classes of finding, ruling and refusal. Byte-identity is explicitly NOT the condition here, because the source is a run rather than a text.
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-15` *(hard)* — The changeset weakens no gate: it introduces no new type-checker suppression and no new linter suppression on changed lines, no new skip / skipif / `pytest.skip(...)` / `importorskip(...)`, and removes no `def test_` declaration and no `assert` line on changed lines. *[stage-2 validator repair 2026-08-12 — "*`make check` *is green" is* `execution_graded`*, a forbidden class of the shipped criteria contract: a command whose EXECUTION is what grades it. Running the gate remains this fire's standing house-rule obligation; it is not an acceptance criterion. The negative-shape proxy above is the form the shipped drafter contract prescribes in its place.]*
- [ ] `KOD-127-AC-16` *(soft)* — A finding this mandate forms is written to the item that owns the surface it concerns at the moment it is formed, carrying its evidence and its interim reading — the parent lane's raise-time ordering consumed unchanged, graded there rather than re-derived here.

**Two halt conditions carried as criteria rather than as prose, because each would otherwise be a decision the implementer invents.** A configuration that restricts the third member's setter to the approver role changes this mandate's dispatch predicate and is ruled by the founder, not by the fire: on that arm the fire HALTS and reports rather than choosing (`KOD-127-AC-3` implements the any-principal arm only). A second definition of anything on the consumed list is a defect on this issue, not a local convenience (`KOD-127-AC-6`).

**Verdict: CLEAN after one regeneration round.** `queue:approved:criteria` set; existing labels preserved.

Independent grader — did not author this set. Validated per the criteria-feasibility contract the composed tree ships. This is the milestone's only fully GENERATED set (the body carries no Verification section), so it was graded harder against invention rather than extraction.

**Per criterion (16):** 15 → `feasible` / repair `none`. `-AC-15` → `infeasible` / repair `criterion_text`, repaired in the body and re-verdicted `feasible`.

**Grounds, re-derived rather than accepted:**
- `-AC-15` ("`make check` is green") is `execution_graded` — a forbidden class. Replaced by the negative-shape proxy the shipped drafter contract prescribes. Running the gate stays this fire's standing house-rule obligation.
- `-AC-3` and `-AC-14` take repair `none`, not `environment_supply`: both grade through the tracker port, which this scope declares as a capability. An escalation staying open on another lane and a class-for-class parity measured against dated ruling comments and groomed footers are both readable through it.
- `-AC-14`'s refusal of byte-identity is correct and is the mirror image of the sibling grooming-template issue, where byte-identity is REQUIRED. The discriminator is real: a text has a byte string, a run does not. Neither issue's treatment can be copied to the other.
- No criterion here re-derives anything on the consumed list; `-AC-6` and `-AC-7` are the negative assertions that keep it that way, which is the right shape for a mandate that owns a table row rather than an organ.

**Observation, not a fault:** `-AC-6` leans on the parent lane's exactly-one-definition-site static check → `literal_count`. Not refuted; but the shipped harness FLAGS this class and forces `soft_signal`, so the criterion carrying this mandate's whole DRY guarantee will leave the hard-gate partition. Filed as a contract finding on the criterion-lifecycle lane.

**Conjunction:** satisfiable. The one apparent contradiction was checked and cleared rather than assumed: `-AC-12` requires this mandate to APPLY structural change, while the parent lane's `-AC-34` requires structural change to be proposal-only. They hold together only because the parent's discipline is narrowed to an approved scope and this mandate is pre-approval — the roadmap's own narrowing. That narrowing is load-bearing for both sets, and an implementation that drops it makes the pair unsatisfiable.

**Halt arms preserved:** the setter-restriction arm remains a halt-and-report rather than a criterion, which is correct — a founder ruling is not something a fire may satisfy.

**Id integrity:** all 16 ids stored verbatim in backticks; no auto-linkification transform observed on any `-AC-` token.

Recorded PROVISIONAL: the top grading tier is quota-exhausted and this pass ran at writer tier. Fresh-context independence holds; tier elevation does not. Every verdict and the repair above is subject to top-tier re-verification — with particular attention owed to the generated set, since nothing upstream constrained it to extracted text.
